brief: A single bowling ball resting on a polished lane, painted in deep candy-apple burgundy over a metal-flake base. Soft spray gradients build the glassy depth, with fine speckle for the flake and a sharp, mirrored window reflection across the crown. Wrapping its curve are lowrider pinstripes: long, tapered, single-stroke lines in lime green and cream that swell and flick into symmetrical scrolls, following the sphere's curvature exactly. The finger holes are crisp, dark and bevelled. The lane's maple boards stretch away in reflection. It is loud, glossy and proud, a custom-shop flourish on an everyday object.

A close view of dish-soap foam piled in a steel kitchen sink, each bubble showing opal-like play-of-colour. Flecks and flashes of electric green, violet, tangerine and peacock blue shift across the milky membranes. Wet-in-wet watercolour lets the iridescence pool and bloom inside each sphere, and crisp pencil arcs mark the bubble walls where they press together. The brushed steel beneath is a cool grey blur. Fresh, everyday, quietly dazzling.

The head of a cockerel is shown in profile and filling the frame, painted hyperreal on a lacquered black ground. Its comb and wattles are cadmium scarlet, waxy and veined. The neck hackles are not rendered as fur. Instead they are built from hundreds of loaded comma strokes in the Petrykivka manner, each tapering from a fat drop to a hair-fine tail. They layer vermilion, saffron and sap green, which becomes the true colour of iridescent feathers. The eye is a glossy amber bead with a pinpoint reflection of a window. The brushwork is confident and rhythmic, decorative in its gesture but photographic in its accumulation.

A rural vending machine beside a flooded rice paddy, painted the way a hand-painted anime background is built. Layered opaque watercolour gives a towering cumulus in cerulean and titanium white, with crisp lilac undersides. The machine is rendered hyperreal: scuffed enamel, a sun-faded cola logo, condensation on the glass, every can label legible behind it. The low horizon sits in the lower third with wide, still air above. Fine pen picks out power lines and paddy reflections. Edges are hard and clean, colour is saturated but airy, and the light is a late-summer afternoon with no people present.

A full-bleed radiograph of a woman's leather handbag, seen as if passed through an airport scanner. The ground is deep Prussian blue-black built from layered charcoal mass. The contents float in ghostly overlap: a ring of keys, a lipstick bullet, a folded umbrella's ribs, a phone's circuit board and loose coins. They glow in graded milky whites and pale cyan where density thickens. Each object is rendered with obsessive accuracy in soft white pencil and fine pen: solder points, spring coils, the zipper's tiny teeth. Edges bloom softly as on film. The composition tilts diagonally and is cropped hard at the corners, clinical and intimate.

Hyperreal pair of tortoiseshell sunglasses lying folded on a Memphis-style plastic laminate tabletop. Squiggles, confetti dashes and terrazzo flecks in bubblegum pink, mint, lemon and black run off every edge at a jaunty tilt. The laminate is flat, saturated alcohol-marker colour with visible streak overlaps. The glasses get obsessive precision: amber-and-umber tortoiseshell mottling in layered marker glazes, and each lens reflects a warped, miniature copy of the pattern in fine pen. Hard daylight leaves one crisp offset shadow. It should feel playful and graphic at a glance, then uncannily photographic up close.

The view from a parked car's driver seat at dawn on the coast. The windshield is covered in hundreds of dew droplets, each a tiny lens holding an inverted, desaturated world. Beyond the glass, a flat marine-layer ceiling sits low and grey-blue over a faint pier. Draw it in coloured pencil on mid-grey toned paper, with white pencil for every droplet's catchlight and soft blending for the overcast. The only warmth is the amber glow of a dashboard dial along the bottom edge. The mood is muted, damp and patient, with an obsessive density of droplets.

A tangerine fibreglass television shaped like an astronaut's helmet sits on a white shag-free terrazzo floor. Its convex grey screen holds a perfectly distorted reflection of a child's wide-eyed face and a sunlit picture window. The rendering is all soft spray gradients, airbrush-smooth, with glossy marker highlights snapped onto the curved plastic in pure white. The palette is optimistic: tangerine, cream, atomic turquoise and chrome silver, under clean bright daylight. The composition is a low worm's-eye view so the set looms like a spacecraft. Mould seams, a fingerprint smudge and tiny dust motes on the screen keep it insistently real rather than illustrated.

A vintage cast-metal gumball machine sits on a checkerboard diner counter. Its glass globe is packed with glossy candy gumballs, and here and there one is a perfectly rendered, wet human eyeball looking back. The palette is carnival-saturated: candy-apple red enamel, bubblegum pink, mint and cream. It is painted with layered markers, with hard specular highlights left as clean paper. Thin hot-rod pinstripe flourishes in black pen curl off the base. The finish is slick and obsessive, like custom kustom-kulture enamel, with a cheeky, unsettling grin to it.

A cast-iron skillet with a single fried egg, seen at a steep three-quarter angle and rendered in pure black ink on off-white with no grey wash. All tone comes from linocut-style gouge marks: swelling, tapering pen strokes that follow the curvature of the pan rim, the domed yolk and the lacy, bubbling egg-white edges. Dense parallel flow-field lines carve the seasoned iron. Bare white flecks mark the oil spatter. The result should read as a photograph from across the room and as carved relief up close. The edges are crisp and the blacks are heavy and solid.

A single brass zipper pull and a short run of interlocking teeth on navy nylon, placed hard off-centre on a flat field of signal red. The design follows strict Swiss grid discipline, with large ruled areas left empty and a thin black rule bar running along one edge. The zip itself is hyperreal: crisp fine-pen teeth, a scratched marker-shaded brass slider with a pinpoint reflection, and frayed thread at the tape edge. There is no gradient anywhere except on the metal. The tension between flat graphic emptiness and microscopic object truth is the whole point.

A parked black bicycle by a rural railway crossing at winter dusk, with fresh snow settled on its saddle, basket and handlebar grips. The sky is a smooth graded wash from Prussian blue down to soft peach at the horizon. Below it lie layered watercolour planes with crisp edges, and falling snow is reserved as tiny white flecks. A fine, confident pen line traces the crossing barrier, the wires and the spokes. Within the woodblock calm, each surface is hyperreal: chipped paint, frozen chain and footprints. It feels lonely and tender, a still moment between trains.

Seen from above, cola spills from a tipped glass across a speckled black granite countertop. The spreading puddle is banded like precipitation returns: concentric spray-mist zones that shift from radar green to yellow to orange to a dense core of crimson where the liquid is deepest. The carbonation bubbles are rendered in hyperreal detail as tiny pen-and-white-marker spheres along the leading edge. The stone flecks stay photographic and cool. The banding follows the true meniscus contours, so the data-overlay colouring and the realism fuse into one surface.

A folding aluminium lawn chair with tangerine and white woven webbing stands on a concrete pool deck. It is seen at noon from a low three-quarter angle, with its razor-sharp shadow cast across the coping. The pool's turquoise water fills the top half, its caustic light lines rendered in exact fine pen. A slice of breeze-block wall sits at one edge. Flat, saturated marker fills meet ruled, hard edges, and every scuff on the tubing and every fraying web strand is precisely observed. The mood is crisp, dry and leisurely, an architectural photograph of idleness.

An audio cassette with a loop of shiny tape spilling out, rendered hyperreal. Its scratched clear casing and screws are sharp, and its chrome-like label reflects a warped grid. Behind it sits a receding wireframe floor in fine pen, with a duotone gradient sky of electric cyan into deep violet. Marker gives slick flat blends, while spray adds grainy photocopy noise and a smudgy halo around the tape's ribbon. The type-free composition is tilted and centred on a starburst. It feels like a crumpled, photocopied flyer found in a jacket pocket, cheap and euphoric.

A hyperreal chrome kettle whose curved body reflects a room. The image is sliced by thick black orthogonal bars into rectangles. Each panel is the same photoreal reflection, but tinted flat cadmium red, cobalt blue, chrome yellow or left white. Smooth marker blending gives the mirror gradients and the warped window highlights. Hard ruled ink lines form the grid. The composition is asymmetric and weighted to the lower right. The rigid grid and the liquid reflections should argue with each other. Light is studio-even and the overall effect is cool and graphic.

Laundry hangs on a rooftop line just after sunset: a white shirt, a striped towel, children's socks. Behind them a city is reduced to dimming silhouettes. The sky is painted in wet-into-wet watercolour from indigo to a thin band of apricot at the horizon. The fabrics are rendered with exact folds and clothespin pressure creases, and they pick up the cool cerulean ambient light. A single warm window glows below, unmistakably tungsten against the blue. Soft charcoal blooms deepen the foreground parapet. The light is fading; the mood is tender, domestic and suspended.

A soap film stretched across a plastic bubble wand, held right up to a child's eye, so the eye's lashes and wet iris are seen through the membrane. The film swirls with thin-film interference bands in magenta, brass gold, cyan and sea green. They are laid as marbled marker flows that drift and pool toward the bottom, where the film thins to black. The eye behind is rendered in crisp coloured pencil, slightly distorted by the curve. A faint spray of window reflections sits on the film. The background is soft out-of-focus kitchen beige.

A tight, tilted view along an accordion's pearloid keyboard and the first folds of its bellows. The keys shimmer with mother-of-pearl swirl, built from burnished coloured pencil in faint shifts of pale pink, celadon, lavender and cream. Directional hatching follows the flaming grain of the nacre. Chrome grille bolts and worn black bellows corners are rendered in dense graphite. Fingerprint smudges and tiny chips in the celluloid sell the realism. The light is soft and lateral, raking across the key edges, and the frame crops abruptly to emphasise rhythm.

A worm's-eye view of an appliance-store wall of stacked microwaves, arranged like plug-in capsules on a megastructure core. Each glowing door window shows a different plate slowly turning: noodles, a mug, a melting butter dish. Technical pen draws the rigid modular grid in precise ruled lines, with steep perspective converging toward the top. Cool grey marker layers build the brushed-steel housings. Small hyperreal vignettes inside each window are coloured in warm amber pencil. The repetition is broken by one open door and one dark, dead unit. The mood is utopian, serial and humming.
